jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer
jobs.description:
QUICK SUMMARY

Own endpoint detection and cloud security at a fully cloud-based company. Tune out the noise, lock down AWS, and build security champions across Kin. 5+ years.




WHO WE ARE

Kin makes life simpler, more affordable, and better for homeowners — especially in the places where climate risks, rising costs, and outdated systems make it harder. We start with smarter homeowners insurance and expand to everything homeowners need to thrive.

Using data, technology, and thoughtful human support, we’re building products that are clear, fair, and help homeowners feel confident — so homeowners aren’t left behind when they need help most.

Founded in 2016, Kin is a remote-first employer with Kinfolk across more than 35 states. We serve customers in 14 states (and counting). Our disciplined growth, strong customer satisfaction, and focus on long-term sustainability fosters outstanding growth, attracts marquee investors, and earns recognition and accolades, including:

 - Built In Chicago's Best Places to Work, Midsize Companies (2021-2026)

 - Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers (2026)

 - Inc. 5000 Fastest-Growing Private Companies

 - Forbes’ Fintech 50 (2023-2026)

 - Great Places to Work Certified (May 2024-May 2027)

Most importantly, we’re building Kin to be a place where people do meaningful work with real impact — for our customers, our communities, and each other. We're excited to tell you more about how you can contribute to our rapid growth, strong unit economics, profitability, and excellent customer ratings. To learn more about how we work and what we’re building, visit kin.com http://kin.com and see how we work https://www.linkedin.com/company/kin-insurance/life/kin/.




THE OPPORTUNITY

We're looking for a Senior Security Engineer to run security operations at Kin. We're remote-first and fully cloud-based, with Kinfolk across more than 35 states working from company laptops and personal devices, signing into everything through SSO. That makes endpoints and identity our front line. Who has access to what, which devices are allowed to touch our data, and how fast we catch it when something goes wrong are the questions this role answers every day.

This is a hands-on role, not a consultative one. You'll own our EDR/MDR stack and the detection tuning, runbooks, and automation that keep a lean team focused on real threats. You'll run endpoint security across managed laptops and BYOD, partner with IT to define the access controls and identity policies that govern our SSO environment, and lead incident response from first alert through containment. You'll also work directly in AWS, building and remediating cloud security controls. And you'll be the person Kinfolk come to with security questions, answering fast enough that people ask rather than guess. Customers trust us with their claims, their property details, and their financial information. Protecting that is the work.




YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own and tune our EDR/MDR stack, building the detection policies, runbooks, and automation that keep escalations focused on real threats

 - Lead incident response end to end: investigation, containment, and remediation, from compromised laptops to cloud and identity incidents

 - Own endpoint security across managed and BYOD devices, setting device posture standards, hardening baselines, and the policies that govern what can access Kin data

 - Define the security requirements behind our identity program and partner with IT to implement them in SSO, shaping our RBAC model and driving an access review cadence that removes stale permissions

 - Build and remediate security controls across AWS infrastructure, Google Workspace, identity, and data protection

 - Serve as the front door for security across Kin, turning around security tickets and questions quickly enough that people bring you things early instead of working around the process

 - Conduct threat modeling across systems, processes, and vendor implementations, delivering risk assessments teams can act on

 - Instill a culture of security across the company, taking everyday opportunities to educate Kinfolk, raise awareness of real risks, and give people in every function the judgment to make safer decisions on their own


Success in this role

In your first 6–12 months at Kin, success is less about checking boxes and more about the impact you create. You’ll use your skills and judgment to take ownership of meaningful work, improve how we operate, and help move Kin’s mission forward. Along the way, you’ll deliver outcomes that make a real difference for both Kinfolk and the homeowners we serve.

By the end of your first year, you should feel confident in your role, trusted as an owner, and proud of the progress you’ve helped make.

 - Detection is tuned and backed by runbooks, so the team's hours go toward investigating real threats instead of triaging noise

 - A clear device posture standard exists, managed devices meet it, and access reviews run with IT on a predictable cadence instead of being a scramble before an audit

 - Cloud vulnerabilities and misconfigurations across AWS and Google Workspace are getting fixed by your own hands, not documented and queued, and the riskiest gaps you inherited are closed

 


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

Technical

 - 5+ years in security operations, detection and response, or security engineering

 - Hands-on experience running a modern EDR program: building and tuning detection logic, writing response runbooks, and leading investigations through to containment

 - Endpoint security experience across managed and BYOD fleets, including device posture, hardening baselines, and MDM

 - Identity and access management depth: defining access control requirements, designing RBAC models, and running access reviews in an SSO environment

 - AWS security experience across IAM, network controls, logging, and configuration management, with a track record of remediating findings directly

 - Comfort working in infrastructure-as-code environments and automating security tasks

 - Threat modeling experience across systems, processes, or vendor implementations

Collaboration and communication

 - A record of fast, reliable responsiveness on security requests, whether that's a ticket queue or someone asking a question in a channel

 - Experience working alongside IT on shared systems, setting security requirements

 - A track record of holding teams accountable for security findings and driving remediation through to completion

 - The ability to explain security risk to non-technical audiences in terms they can act on, so people across the company bring you problems early rather than working around you

Bonus if you have

 - Terraform and CI/CD pipeline experience

 - Zero trust networking experience, including designing or operating identity-aware and device-aware access controls

 - Working knowledge of NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and SOX, and how regulatory compliance translates into engineering requirements

 - Experience securing a fully remote workforce

 - Experience building security awareness or training programs for a non-technical audience

 - Google Workspace security administration experience

 - Security certifications such as AWS Certified Security Specialty, GCIH, or GCIA





HOW WE HIRE

We believe a great hiring experience should be clear, respectful, and human. We’ll accept applications for this position until October 15, 2026. While our recruiting team uses AI tools for efficiency, resumes are still screened by Kin’s in-house recruiters, and candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are made by recruiters and hiring teams. Rest assured, real people make real decisions.

The hiring process and timeline for each role will vary, depending on the position. However, here are some things you can expect from us:

 - Prompt updates and feedback following interviews

 - Interviews with recruiters, hiring managers, and members of teams

 - Skills assessment relevant to the position, if applicable

 - Genuine, thoughtful human interaction at every step




HOW WE SUPPORT YOU

We offer a comprehensive, competitive benefits program, allowing you to choose the benefits that are best for you and your family, starting on the first day of the month following your start date.

Core Benefits

 - Competitive salary and company equity through Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), granted as part of our standard compensation package and based on role and level

 - 401(k) with company match up to 4% of eligible earnings

 - Multiple medical plan options, plus dental and vision coverage

 - Company-funded HSA contributions (based on medical plan selection)

 - Company-paid life insurance and short-term disability

Health & Wellbeing

 - A variety of supplemental benefit options, including long-term disability, critical illness, accident, legal, and pet insurance

 - Access to mental health support and confidential counseling resources

 - Flexible PTO for exempt employees (most employees take 15–20 days per year), plus 8 company-observed holidays

 - Paid parental leave, including up to 14 weeks at 100% pay for birthing parents and 8 weeks at 100% pay for non-birthing parents

Growth & Development

 - Career mobility and internal growth opportunities across the organization

 - Professional development budgets for certifications, conferences, and learning available, subject to management approval




HOW WE WORK

We don’t just hire for skills. We hire for alignment. Kinfolk bring diverse perspectives, but we’re united by a shared set of values that shape how we work and how we show up for each other and our customers.

Run through walls, together - Every one of us is responsible for creating the culture we want to work in. High performance. Low drama. Always respectful. We assume the best in each other and challenge ideas, not intentions. We show up, work hard, and play to each other's strengths — because that’s how great teams win.

Raise the bar. Drop the ego - Attitudes are contagious. Every one of us is responsible for creating the culture we want to work in. High performance. Low drama. Always respectful. Like professional sports teams, we win by working in sync. We show up, work hard, and play to each other’s strengths.

Act like an owner - We are owners, fully accountable for achieving Kin’s mission. That requires positive, proactive, big-picture thinking well beyond our job descriptions. Ask questions, Take ownership. Do the right thing, even when it‘s hard. Because when Kin thrives, so do you. And so do our customers.

Operate lean. Deliver more - We build efficiency into everything we do. Each dollar we save gets reinvested to deliver more to our customers: better pricing, more products, and new innovations. We work smarter by relentlessly prioritizing and using technology, including AI, to multiply our impact. Lean is about focus, not deprivation. Lean isn't a limitation — it's our competitive advantage.

Keep asking ‘What if?’ - We value curiosity. To make insurance better for our customers, we experiment. We embrace insights. And we base decisions on data rather than assumptions. We see setbacks as opportunities for growth and are always learning and improving. Both individually and as a company.




WHERE WE WORK

We are a remote-first company with offices in Chicago, IL and St. Petersburg, FL where teams can come together for collaboration.

For Sales Agents and Customer Service Agents: These roles sit in any of the following 32 states: AL, AZ, CO, FL, ID, IL, IN, KS, KY, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MO, MT, NC, NE, NM, NV, NY, OH, OK, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VT, VA, WA, and WI.

For all other positions, these roles can sit in any of the following 41 states: AL, AR, AZ, CA (exempt only), CO, CT, FL, GA, ID, IL, IN, IA, KS, KY, LA, MA, ME, MD, MI, MN, MO, MT, NC, NE, NJ, NM, NV, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VT, VA, WA, and WI. Please only apply if you are able to live and work full-time in one of the states listed above.

For remote technical positions located in Canada, we are only able to hire individuals who reside in Ontario. Applicants must be able to live and work full-time in Ontario to be considered.

State locations and specifics are subject to change as our hiring requirements shift.




EEOC STATEMENT

Kin is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. We don't just accept difference – we honor it, nurture it, and celebrate it. We don’t discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. Kin welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. jobs.title: RVP, PBM Enterprise Sales
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE:

The RVP, PBM Enterprise Sales is a member of the Rightway Commercial team, reporting into the VP, Head of PBM Enterprise. Our innovative, full-stack pharmacy benefit management (PBM) offering represents an important growth area for Rightway. Through modern technology, concierge pharmacist guidance, and a fully aligned pricing model, Rightway is improving the member experience and helping clients better manage pharmacy spend to make drugs more affordable for their employees and dependents.

Rightway's modern PBM combines transparent, aligned economics with integrated clinical guidance to deliver a radically improved pharmacy experience. We are redefining how employers think about PBM partnerships.

This role is ideal for someone who pairs strategic thinking with disciplined execution. The RVP is responsible for directly selling our PBM solution to self-funded employers (5-20k lives) by developing channel relationships, sourcing new client prospects, and managing complex, multi-stakeholder deals from start to finish. Success in this role requires someone who approaches their territory like a business: organized, data-driven, and thoughtful in how they structure, prioritize, and advance deals, while maintaining the curiosity and creativity to adapt in a fast-changing market.

This position will have a direct impact on the overall growth and success of Rightway, helping further our mission of being a category-defining healthcare technology company.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

• Call on self-funded employer groups of 5-20k lives, third party administrators, brokers, consultants, and coalitions to sell our pharmacy benefit management (PBM) solution within your assigned territory. This segment represents one of Rightway's fastest-growing and most strategically important markets.

• Collaborate with Commercial leadership to develop and execute a direct-to-prospect strategy, managing complex deals from initial discovery through RFP and finalist stages with strategic precision and strong internal coordination.

• Identify, source, and build relationships with new client prospects and channel partners, managing discovery and solution development, pricing recommendations, proposals, and finalist presentations end to end.

• Apply strategic deal management to structure pricing, contracting, and solution design that balances client needs, financial outcomes, and operational readiness.

• Work collaboratively with internal departments such as underwriting, marketing, strategic partnerships, product, implementation, and customer success teams to develop go-to-market strategies and efficiencies to successfully onboard new clients.

• Finalize contract terms and support the accurate translation of the proposal into a contractual agreement.

• Maintain a disciplined, well-documented sales process in Salesforce, using data and forecasting accuracy to track and report sales activity to company leaders and manage deals from discovery to close.

• Participate in and attend business events, conferences, trade shows, and seminars.

WHO YOU ARE:

• 5+ years of direct PBM sales experience, ideally selling to self-funded employers, TPAs, brokers, or consultants. Candidates with 5+ years as a pharmacy benefits consultant advising employers on PBM strategy and procurement will also be considered, with direct PBM sales experience the strong preference.

• 2+ years managing consultant and broker relationships, with demonstrated knowledge of employer, TPA, broker, and consultant buying processes.

• Working knowledge of PBM economic models and deal structure, including rebate mechanics, admin fee/PMPM pricing, aligned vs. spread economics, and performance guarantee structures, and the ability to translate that knowledge into a client-specific deal design.

• Proven track record within PBM sales and/or upsells driving year-over-year profitable growth and client retention, with strong business acumen managing complex, multi-stakeholder deals in a structured, disciplined sales process.

• Current and substantive knowledge of PBM competitors.

• Willing to travel ~30%, depending on the needs of the territory and selling cycle, with proficiency in Google Suite, Microsoft Office, Salesforce, and other industry-related software.

EXTRA CREDIT:

• Direct PBM sales experience with demonstrated success against quota

• PharmD or RPh

COMPENSATION:  $160,000 - $190,000 annually, in addition to bonus and equity

Compensation offered will be determined by geographic location, experience, and qualifications.

CYBERSECURITY AWARENESS NOTICE

In response to ongoing and industry-wide fraudulent recruitment activities (i.e., job scams), Rightway wants to inform potential candidates that we will only contact them from the @rightwayhealthcare.com email domain. We will never ask for bank details or deposits of any kind as a condition of employment.

ABOUT RIGHTWAY:

Rightway is on a mission to harmonize healthcare for everyone, everywhere. Our products guide patients to the best care and medications by inserting clinicians and pharmacists into a patient’s care journey through a modern, mobile app. Rightway is a front door to healthcare, giving patients the tools they need along with on-demand access to Rightway health guides, human experts that answer their questions and manage the frustrating parts of healthcare for them.

Since its founding in 2017, Rightway has raised over $200mm from investors including Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital, and Tiger Global. We’re headquartered in New York City, with satellite offices in Denver and Dallas. Our clients rely on us to transform the healthcare experience, improve outcomes for their teams, and decrease their healthcare costs.

HOW WE LIVE OUR VALUES TO OUR TEAMMATES:

We’re seeking those with passion for healthcare and relentless devotion to our goal. We need team members that embody our core values:

1) We are human, first
Our humanity binds us together. We bring the same empathetic approach to every individual we engage with, whether it be our members, our clients, or each other. We are all worthy of respect and understanding and we engage in our interactions with care and intention. We honor our stories. We listen to—and hear—each other, we celebrate our differences and similarities, we are present for each other, and we strive for mutual understanding.

2) We redefine what is possible
We always look beyond the obstacles in front of us to imagine new solutions. We approach our work with inspiration from other industries, other leaders, and other challenges. We use ingenuity and resourcefulness when faced with tough problems.

3) We debate then commit
We believe that a spirit of open discourse is part of a healthy culture. We understand and appreciate different perspectives and we challenge our assumptions. When working toward a decision or a new solution, we actively listen to one another, approach it with a “yes, and” mentality, and assume positive intent. Once a decision is made, we align and champion it as one team.

4) We cultivate grit
Changing healthcare doesn’t happen overnight. We reflect and learn from challenges and approach the future with a determination to strive for better. In the face of daunting situations, we value persistence. We embrace failure as a stepping stone to future success. On this journey, we seek to act with guts, resilience, initiative, and tenacity.

5) We seek to delight
Healthcare is complicated and personal. We work tirelessly to meet the goals of our clients while also delivering the best experience to our members. We recognize that no matter the role or team, we each play a crucial part in our members’ care and take that responsibility seriously. When faced with an obstacle, we are kind, respectful, and solution-oriented in our approach. We hold ourselves accountable to our clients and our members’ success.

Rightway is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer that believes in the strength of diverse thought, beliefs, backgrounds, and education. We foster an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated to drive the best business decisions possible. We do not discriminate on any basis protected by applicable law. All employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, need, and performance.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Fall Co-Op
jobs.description:
Halo is a hair technology company using breakthrough engineering to elevate everyday routines. We’re building the world’s first robotic hair-braiding system—integrating computer vision, robotics, compliant fiber manipulation, and novel mechatronic machines. This is one of the hardest unsolved problems in robotics, applied to a $300B industry.



8 billion hours are spent braiding hair each year. HaloBraid gives that time back. The system collaborates with professional stylists to reduce braiding appointments from 6 hours to minutes and grow their business. We’re moving from R&D into deployment with salons, well-funded by leading investors. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of the hair styling industry.

We are looking for a Spring 2027 Mechanical Engineering Co-op to play a pivotal role in developing our innovative hair braiding robotic system.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - ﻿﻿Contribute to the development of complex technology, product sub-assemblies, and test rigs

 - ﻿﻿Take an active, hands-on role to ensure that engineering problems are resolved thoroughly

 - ﻿﻿Utilize various rapid prototyping technologies to build, test, and iterate

 - ﻿﻿Use hand calculations, computer simulation, and/or lab-based testing to validate designs through the development process

 - ﻿﻿Conduct user testing and project the voice of the customer back into the design

 - Conduct various forms of testing, problem solving, and design iteration


REQUIREMENTS:

 - ﻿﻿At least one semester remaining in your undergraduate or graduate degree

 - ﻿﻿Experience with CAD (we use Onshape, experience with Solidworks or equivalent is acceptable)

 - ﻿﻿Experience with various rapid prototyping methods (3D printing, CNC, etc)

 - ﻿﻿Demonstrated design intelligence, mechanical intuition, creative problem solving, and strong attention to detail

 - ﻿﻿A willingness to fail and learn!
   
   


DESIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE (OPTIONAL BUT THE MORE, THE BETTER)

 - ﻿﻿Gone through (and documented!) the design process for a project, through school or on your own time

 - ﻿﻿Strong documentation skills and the ability to convey complex ideas in a team setting

 - Strong experimental rigor and testing process

 - Experience with complex CAD models with clear top down design

 - ﻿﻿Experience with consumer electronics, robotics, or hair styling tools

 - ﻿﻿Interest in hair braiding/styling

 - Interest in robotics and mechanisms

 - Complementary engineering experience:
   
   - Mechanisms, mechatronics, and moving components.
   
   - ﻿﻿Experience with design optimization using FEA/CFD simulation
   
   - Electronics prototyping and soldering
     
     

Working Style

 - User centric, you want to build stuff people use and love

 - Low ego, adaptable, and collaborative spirit

 - Willing to learn through fast-paced iteration and feedback

 - Passionate, driven by innovation
   
   

Benefits of Working with Us:

 - Company subsidized parking or commute for onsite employees



Onsite work

This is an onsite full time position at our office/lab in Cambridge, MA. You must have authorization to work in the US.



Don’t Meet Every Requirement?

If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align with every single part of the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway.

jobs.title: Hospice Medical Social Worker – LMSW or LCSW
jobs.description:
About the Role

Provide compassionate, clinical psychosocial care that helps patients and families navigate the emotional, social, and practical challenges of end-of-life illness. As a Hospice Medical Social Worker, you'll support individuals facing terminal diagnoses by offering counseling, guidance, and resources that promote dignity, clarity, and emotional well-being during one of life’s most difficult transitions.

This role is ideal for a licensed clinical social worker who is passionate about practicing the full scope of hospice social work in a deeply meaningful setting. You’ll complete comprehensive psychosocial assessments, provide crisis intervention and counseling, and support advance care planning conversations that help families make informed, values-based decisions. Working as a key member of the interdisciplinary team, you’ll collaborate closely with nurses, physicians, and other hospice professionals to ensure emotional, cultural, and practical needs are fully integrated into each patient’s plan of care. Your work will directly support both patients and families while also strengthening the care experience across the entire hospice journey.

Location

• Office Location: 600 E Carmel Dr. Suite 144, Carmel, IN 46032

• Main Service Area: Boone, Clinton, Hamilton, Hancock, Hendricks, Johnson, Madison, Marion, Morgan, Shelby

• This role is a high travel position and requires daily travel within the service area to provide care to patients in their homes, assisted living facilities, or nursing homes

Hours

• Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Required Qualification

• Master's or doctoral degree from a CSWE-accredited school of social work

• Current State License as a Master's Social Worker (MSW/LMSW/LCSW)

• Minimum 1 year of experience as a licensed Master's Social Worker

• Reliable transportation, valid driver’s license, and valid automobile insurance coverage

• Willingness to travel to homes, facilities, and community settings

Preferred Qualifications

• Hospice or palliative care experience

• Clinical experience with grief counseling and end-of-life issues

• Knowledge of Medicare hospice benefit and Conditions of Participation

Essential Skills and Competencies

• Strong clinical counseling and grief support skills

• Expertise in psychosocial assessment and crisis intervention

• Ability to guide patients and families through end-of-life challenges

• Excellent communication skills with emotional intelligence

• Cultural sensitivity and competence working with diverse populations

• Knowledge of community resources and social service systems

• Strong interdisciplinary collaboration abilities

• Understanding of family systems and dynamics

• Ability to maintain professional boundaries while providing empathetic support

• Deep commitment to hospice philosophy of care

Pay Range

$70,000—$75,000 USD

How We Care for You

• Mileage Reimbursement

• Minimum of 3 Weeks Paid Time Off for Full Time

• Part Time/Per Diem also accrue Paid Time Off

• Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance

• HSA and FSA options including Dependent Care

• Company paid Short Term Disability

• Company paid Life Insurance

• 401(k) with Employer Match

• Pet Insurance

• ID and Fraud Protection

• And more...

Optimal Care is where your dedication meets a rewarding career.

Top Work Places for 12 consecutive years, Great Places to Work certified for 6 consecutive years, and we believe that exceptional care starts with exceptional people. We’re committed to supporting your professional growth, valuing your expertise, and creating an environment where you can do your best work every day.

As a clinician-owned and operated organization, we empower our team members to provide personalized, compassionate care to patients and families every day.

We are a leading provider of Physician Services, Home Health, and Hospice that encourages collaboration, innovation, and clinical excellence. From chronic disease management and rehabilitation to end-of-life care, our focus is on improving outcomes and enhancing quality of life.

We live a simple Mission: Serve Together, Provide Value, and Deliver Exceptional Quality Care.

Background Screening

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
OUR MISSION:

At Sunrise Robotics, we are dedicated to augmenting humanity through intelligent robotics. Our mission is to elevate the world of manufacturing by introducing intelligent, flexible robots that enhance human capabilities and existing machinery, ushering in the next era of production at higher quality, with less waste, and lower cost.



OUR VISION:

We see a future where every element of manufacturing, from design to assembly, is optimised with intelligent automation. Our vision is to integrate flexible robotic solutions, based on generic hardware and advanced software/AI capabilities, into manufacturing, particularly in small and medium-sized enterprises, to make automation economically viable and accessible, for all sizes of manufacturers. We are not just building robots; we are creating the strategically crucial components for autonomous, intelligent agents of the future.

The role

We are hiring a Chief of Staff to the CEO.

You are the CEO's closest execution partner. You sit in the rooms the CEO sits in, and represent him in the ones he cannot be in. You make sure the company executes fast on the decisions made in those rooms, by driving the most important cross-team projects yourself.

The mandate has four parts. Run the operating cadence the leadership team works inside. Own the company's commitments and see them through to done. Make the CEO's decisions and priorities legible to everyone they affect. Protect the CEO's time for the work only the CEO can do.

This is a senior individual role with no direct reports. Your authority comes from the mandate, agreed in writing with the CEO, and from being right. You are not a gatekeeper.

We are outcome-driven, direct, high trust and high autonomy. There is very little hand-holding. We enjoy working with people who bring a healthy degree of intensity and drive.

What this role is not

Not an executive assistant. Not a COO. Not a strategy seat where you write decks about work other people do.

What you will do

 - Run the operating cadence
   Own the quarterly planning cycle, company goals and the weekly leadership meeting: agenda, a dashboard of under 15 metrics, decisions written down, commitments tracked to done. Every red metric gets a root cause and an owner within the week.

 - Drive cross-functional execution
   When a decision needs three teams and has no single owner, you are the direct responsible individual until it lands. You hold owners to their dates, unblock, and escalate early. Most of these run in weeks, not quarters.

 - Make decisions travel
   Every leadership decision gets written down and reaches the people it affects within a day. You draft the all-hands deck, decision memos and internal communication in the CEO's voice. The CEO edits; you draft. You hold the bar in the rooms the CEO is not in. When quality or pace drops, you name it that day.

 - Build and manage the operating system
   Morning briefs, commitments tracking, meeting-to-action pipelines, and the reporting the CEO takes to the board. Build the foundation and systems, so the company gets more legible with less manual work. You do this yourself, not through a vendor.

 - Make the company legible
   Decisions, processes and playbooks written once, findable by everyone, and used as the standard.

 - Take special projects, up to a day a week
   You pick them up with CEO-level urgency and hand them back completed, or with an owner and a clear path to done.

Who you are

 - You bring energy
   High intensity, high pace, and you are impatient when good decisions sit. You set the tempo in a room without raising your voice. People move faster because you are there.

 - You have operated inside a fast-changing, venture-backed company
   Typically four to eight years in. You have lived through at least one moment where the plan changed under you and you kept the team executing. Titles vary: chief of staff, business operations, founder's associate, program or product lead, consultant who went operating, ex-founder. We care about the work, not the title.

 - You build systems, not just tasks
   Somewhere, a team runs on a cadence or a tool you set up, and it kept working after you left the room.

 - You think in systems
   You see how a change in hiring shows up in deploy capacity three months later. You spot the second-order effect before it hits.

 - You run complex projects across stakeholders
   Several teams, outside parties, a hard deadline, no formal authority. You have done that and landed it.

 - You are technically fluent
   Strong technical fluency is required. You are equally at home in a spreadsheet and a database. You pull your own numbers, build your own model, and follow an engineering discussion closely enough to ask the question that matters.

 - You are AI-native
   You have built agents or automations that run without you: a pipeline, a briefing, a tracker. You can show us. Daily use of a chatbot is not enough.

 - You write and visualize information clearly
   Short, clear, and in someone else's voice when needed. A one-page memo from you ends a debate. You turn data into the chart that makes the decision obvious.

 - You chase without being annoying
   Following up daily is the job. People end up grateful you did.

 - You hold confidences
   You will know about sensitive information before almost anyone. That access is a duty, not a way to be liked.

 - You push back
   You get to the real intent behind a vague request and say when we are wrong. You argue from facts.

 - You are curious about the actual work
   You want to know what a deploy engineer does in a customer's facility at 6am, and you go and find out.

Bonus points

 - You have shipped something with Claude Code, Codex or similar, and can talk about what broke.

 - You have worked in hardware, robotics or manufacturing, where part of the team works next to the machines.

Location

Remote within Europe. For the first six months you spend up to half your time in Ljubljana, next to the CEO. After that, remote with regular travel to Ljubljana.

Why Sunrise?

 - Work directly with the CEO, founders and leadership at an early stage, in a role that touches every decision the company makes.

 - We care about talent density, speed of execution and long-term technology leverage.

 - Get things done, and you shape your own trajectory.

jobs.title: Operator III
jobs.description:
Position Purpose:

The Operator III is responsible for supporting the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of a reciprocating engine-based power generation facility consisting of multiple engine-generator units and associated balance-of-plant (BOP) systems. This role performs routine operational activities, monitors plant equipment, and assists in maintaining optimal plant performance while ensuring compliance with all safety, environmental, and operational requirements.

The Operator III works closely with the Shift Supervisor, Instrumentation & Electrical (I&E) Technicians, Maintenance Technicians, OEM representatives, contractors, and vendors to support plant availability, equipment reliability, commissioning activities, startup and shutdown operations, troubleshooting, and planned outages. This position requires strong mechanical aptitude, attention to detail, sound judgment, and a commitment to safe work practices in a high-reliability power generation environment.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

• Safely start, stop, operate, and monitor engine-generator packages and all associated auxiliary equipment in accordance with OEM specifications, plant procedures, and operating limits.
• Monitor plant equipment through the control system and field inspections to ensure safe and reliable operation.
• Adjust operating parameters and setpoints within approved OEM and plant guidelines to optimize performance, efficiency, and equipment reliability.
• Conduct routine equipment inspections and document operating conditions, equipment status, and abnormalities.
• Identify, troubleshoot, and report equipment malfunctions or abnormal operating conditions to the Shift Supervisor.
• Assist with plant startups, shutdowns, commissioning activities, and planned maintenance outages.
• Coordinate with Maintenance and I&E personnel to safely isolate equipment and return systems to service following maintenance activities.
• Complete operating logs, shift reports, inspections, and other required documentation accurately and in a timely manner.
• Participate in OEM and company training programs to develop a thorough understanding of plant systems, operating procedures, and equipment capabilities.
• Follow all company safety policies, environmental regulations, permit-to-work procedures, lockout/tagout (LOTO), confined space, and other safe work practices.
• Maintain high standards of housekeeping throughout the facility to promote a safe and organized work environment.
• Assist contractors, OEM representatives, and vendors while work is performed on site.
• Respond appropriately to plant alarms, emergency situations, and abnormal operating conditions.
• Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance plant safety, reliability, and operational efficiency.
• Perform other duties as assigned by the Shift Supervisor or Plant Management.

Work Environment:

• Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions.
• Ability to work around high-voltage equipment, rotating machinery, elevated noise levels, and hot surfaces while following all applicable safety procedures.

Education/Experience/Background:

• High School Diploma or GED required.
• Previous experience in industrial operations, manufacturing, utilities, oil and gas, or power generation is preferred but not required.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

• Basic understanding of mechanical equipment, pumps, compressors, engines, valves, and auxiliary systems.
• Ability to read and interpret operating procedures, equipment manuals, and technical documentation.
• Basic computer skills and ability to use plant monitoring and reporting systems.
• Strong communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.
• Commitment to maintaining a safe work environment.
• Ability to recognize abnormal equipment conditions and respond appropriately.
• Mechanical aptitude with the ability to learn complex plant systems.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
• Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
• Ability to prioritize tasks in a fast-paced operating environment.
• Willingness to work rotating shifts, weekends, holidays, overtime, and respond to emergency callouts as required.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training:

• Technical training or coursework in power generation, industrial operations, mechanical systems, or a related field preferred.

Physical Requirements:

• Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
• Ability to climb stairs and ladders and work at elevated heights.
• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.
• Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, and flame-resistant clothing.

Benefits: Veolia’s comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

Disclaimer: The salary, other compensation, and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, subject to applicable law.

jobs.title: Staff Mask Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

We are looking for an experienced Staff Mask Design Engineer to join a highly skilled layout organization working on Analog and Mixed-Signal ICs for Automotive applications. The role involves defining, developing, and delivering high-quality, manufacturable IC layouts using industry-standard technologies and tools.

The successful candidate will contribute at block and Chip top level, lead layout activities, collaborate closely with design and cross-functional teams, and ensure robust physical implementation that meets performance, reliability, and quality requirements.

Job Purpose:

The purpose of this role is to deliver robust, high-quality physical layouts for complex analog and mixed-signal ICs, ensuring manufacturability, reliability, and on-time delivery, while contributing to layout methodology, team capability, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities:

As a Staff Mask Design Engineer, you will be responsible for:

· Implementing physical layouts for Automotive Business Line products at IP, block, and/or Chip Top level.

· Driving and delivering floorplanning activities for blocks and top-level designs.

· Participating in power supply strategy definition and signal distribution between blocks.

· Delivering analog and mixed-signal layout blocks and contributing to top-level floorplan strategy.

· Applying state-of-the-art layout techniques for device matching, parasitic reduction, ESD protection, latch-up prevention, and yield optimization.

· Executing and signing off physical verification flows, including DRC, LVS, ERC, DFM, and parasitic extraction (PEX).

· Working according to Analog-on-Top and Mixed-Signal-on-Top layout methodologies.

· Attending relevant project and design reviews, reporting progress, risks, and schedule impacts.

· Collaborating closely with design, verification, CAD, and technology teams to minimize rework and resolve physical implementation issues.

· Identifying root causes and proposing solutions for issues observed during first silicon or prototype evaluation.

· Contributing to design-for-quality, ensuring layouts are verified, validated, and suitable for long-term reliability and zero-defect goals.

· Leading layout team activities, including task planning, execution, and knowledge sharing.

· Participating in and contributing to training activities, technical documentation, and layout guidelines.

· Taking a proactive role in personal development, continuous learning, and methodology improvement.

· Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical, Electronics, or Microelectronics Engineering.

· 8+ years of experience in Analog and Mixed-Signal IC layout design.

· Proven experience delivering complex layouts at IP, block, and Chip Top level.

· Experience in automotive or safety-critical semiconductor products is highly desirable.

Technical Skills:

· Strong expertise in analog layout techniques, including:

o Floorplanning and top-level integration

o Device matching and symmetry

o Parasitic management

o Latch-up prevention and ESD protection

· Solid understanding of electronics, semiconductor physics, and fabrication processes.

· Hands-on expertise with layout and verification tools, including:

o Cadence Virtuoso / Virtuoso XL (OA, PVS)

o Mentor Graphics Calibre (DRC, LVS, PEX, DFM)

o R3D and related parasitic extraction tools

· Experience with advanced CMOS BCD technologies

· Experience using Mixed-Signal-on-Top (MSoT) flows

· Ability to define and execute advanced floorplan strategies

Soft Skills & Ways of Working:

· Strong team player, self-motivated, and results-oriented.

· Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multisite, multicultural environment.

· Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.

· Clear, concise communication and presentation skills.

· Ability to propose innovative and pragmatic solutions.

· Strong focus on quality, reliability, and on-time delivery.

· Willingness to undertake occasional international travel if required.

· Comfortable collaborating with cross-functional teams including design, test, program management, and quality.

Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier. With a global team of over 21,000 engineers and problem solvers in more than 30 countries, we offer the opportunity to work on world‑leading technology for Automotive, Industrial, Infrastructure, and IoT, shaping a safer, healthier, greener, and smarter future.

At Renesas, TAGIE is our culture, grounded in being Transparent, Agile, Global, Innovative, and Entrepreneurial. It shapes how we work, grow and deliver on our purpose together. This collaborative spirit and mindset drive our semiconductor technology to transform industries and impact millions of lives.

We believe in rewarding our employees with a competitive benefits package alongside their salary. More information will be provided during the hiring process.

jobs.title: Team Lead, People Technology
jobs.description:
DRW is a diversified trading firm with over 3 decades of experience bringing sophisticated technology and exceptional people together to operate in markets around the world. We value autonomy and the ability to quickly pivot to capture opportunities, so we operate using our own capital and trading at our own risk.

Headquartered in Chicago with offices throughout the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia, we trade a variety of asset classes including Fixed Income, ETFs, Equities, FX, Commodities and Energy across all major global markets. We have also leveraged our expertise and technology to expand into three non-traditional strategies: real estate, venture capital and cryptoassets.

We operate with respect, curiosity and open minds. The people who thrive here share our belief that it’s not just what we do that matters–it's how we do it. DRW is a place of high expectations, integrity, innovation and a willingness to challenge consensus.

The Team:
HR functions across the firm — Talent Acquisition, Talent Development, Talent Management, and others — rely on a growing suite of purpose-built internal applications to run critical people processes: campus recruiting quizzes, candidate pipeline integrations, interactive trading games for recruiting events, onboarding forms, in-office trend tracking, peer recognition, and more. Today, these applications are maintained across the broader Infrastructure Development team without a dedicated, product-minded owner. We are launching Infrastructure Development - People Technology, a new sub-team within Infrastructure Development, to serve as the dedicated engineering partner to HR. People Technology will own the full lifecycle of eight internal applications spanning the talent lifecycle — from recruiting and onboarding through recognition and engagement.

The Role:
We are seeking a Lead / Senior Engineer to serve as the founding member and technical leader of the People Technology team. You will be the single point of ownership for the team's entire application suite, and the primary engineering partner to HR stakeholders across Talent Acquisition, Talent Development, Talent Management, and HR Leadership. This is not a pure management role — you will be hands-on in the code while simultaneously shaping the team's roadmap, building relationships across HR, and standing up the team from scratch.
As the first hire, you will also validate our initial staffing assumptions and partner with leadership to scope and fill the team's second engineering role.

Key Responsibilities:

• Own the technical direction and roadmap for a suite of eight HR-adjacent applications, balancing maintenance and stability with new feature development driven by HR partner priorities.

• Serve as the primary engineering point of contact for HR stakeholders — embedding in their planning sessions, understanding their pain points, and translating business needs into technical solutions.

• Conduct a comprehensive assessment across all applications — evaluating tech debt, modernization opportunities, support burden, and alignment with engineering standards.

• Validate the team's initial staffing model and partner with leadership to define and fill the second engineering role.

• Write and ship production code across a diverse stack (Python, TypeScript/React, Ruby, FastAPI, Flask, Next.js, PostgreSQL) while maintaining high quality standards.

• Formalize support processes, stakeholder communication channels, and operational workflows as the team matures.

Required Qualifications:

• Strong full-stack engineering background with hands-on experience across Python, TypeScript/React, and PostgreSQL.

• Proven ability to own and drive multiple applications end-to-end — from roadmap through delivery and support.

• Experience partnering directly with non-technical business stakeholders to translate needs into technical solutions.

• Comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy — this is a founding role where you will define processes, priorities, and team culture from scratch.

• Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset — you will spend as much time in conversations with HR partners as you will writing code.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience with Ruby/Sinatra, FastAPI, Flask, or Next.js.

• Prior experience in a technical lead or team lead capacity, including mentoring junior engineers.

• Familiarity with HR systems and workflows (e.g., applicant tracking systems, HRIS platforms) or similar enterprise integrations.

The annual base salary range for this position is $140,000 to $180,000 depending on the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and relevant skill set. The position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. In addition, DRW offers a comprehensive suite of employee benefits including group medical, pharmacy, dental and vision insurance, 401k (with discretionary employer match), short and long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance, health savings accounts, and flexible spending accounts.

For more information about DRW's processing activities and our use of job applicants' data, please view our Privacy Notice at https://drw.com/privacy-notice.

California residents, please review the California Privacy Notice for information about certain legal rights at https://drw.com/california-privacy-notice.

SUMMARY:
The Federal Project Executive performs Management of multiple BRPH projects and defined customer programs with the Departments of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, as well as other select federal organizations. Leads strategic architectural/engineering design projects from concept through construction documentation, while ensuring compliance with client requirements. Oversees project managers delivering architectural/engineering design projects while serving as the client-facing executive, ensuring design integrity, technical excellence, financial success, and prudent risk management, while adhering to BRPH’s Mission and Vision.

As part of the federal business unit, supports the development of new business and generates sales in keeping with annual company and individual goals for BRPH Architects and Engineers. Proactively initiates and maintains client contact, cultivates potential client and local strategic partnerships and relationships with key decision-makers and implements public relations and business development activities that are continually effective and competitive. Interfaces with clients and project teams to ensure successful outcomes and repeat business. Leverages client trust to drive repeat business and expanded project roles for BRPH.

•    Effective communication skills, with executive presence
•    Mentorship, integrity, professionalism
•    Adaptable, resilient, results-driven, and aligned with firm core values
•    Promotes continuous improvement and supports best practices and standards by the BRPH Project Management Office (PMO).

REQUIRED COMPETENCIES:
•    Project Management Mastery: Strong in scope management, scheduling, budgeting, earned value, resource planning, and risk control.
•    Strategic Thinking: Ability to link design decisions to client goals and business outcomes.
•    Communication & Influence: Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to present convincingly to executives, lead alignment, and manage stakeholder consensus.
•    Problem Solving: Sound judgment, ability to break down complex issues, weigh trade-offs, and make timely decisions.
•    Financial Acumen: Understanding forecasting, profitability, cost control, and managing change orders/additional services.

•    Ensures that each discipline meets deliverable timelines and maintain cross-discipline coordination to avoid rework.
•    Identifies project risks and issues proactively; maintains a risk register; leads risk mitigation planning.
•    Leads all project coordination meetings, maintains decision and issues logs, produces regular status updates (schedule, cost, risk, design progress).
•    Conducts QA/QC reviews, enforces compliance with codes, standards, firm processes, and reduces rework.
•    Drives project close-out: ensures final deliverables, meets quality and completeness, facilitates lessons-learned sessions, documents best practices for continuous improvement.
•    Provides vision, direction, and alignment to design leads and discipline teams, clearly linking project goals to design execution.
•    Mentors and coaches design staff and early career project managers, helping their professional growth, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and technical development.
•    Supports Federal Business Unit Leader with the development and execution of sales and marketing activities necessary to penetrate targeted business segments and maintain a robust sales funnel of potential opportunities with short-and long-range goals. Contributes to development of annual business plans and growth targets.

•    Functions as communications link between the client and internal BRPH team for all new business activity.

•    Engages in occasional travel for client site meetings, design reviews, and stakeholder engagements.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE:

•    Bachelor’s degree in architecture or engineering, from an accredited four-year college or university.
•    Ten years of experience as project manager, with preferred experience in delivering projects to federal clients, primarily to Department of War (DoW), including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Army Installation Management Command (IMCOM), Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC), Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC), and/or (DoW) installations.
•    Proficient with operating a personal computer and use of Deltek Vantagepoint or similar project management software, MS Excel/Word/Outlook/Teams/Power Point, Bluebeam, and other required programs.

CERTIFICATE, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:
•    Registered/licensed architect or engineer is highly preferred;
•    Bachelor’s degree in architecture or engineering.
•    Ten years of experience as project manager, seller-doer type role.
•    Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is a strong differentiator, but not mandatory
•    Proficient with operating a personal computer and use of Deltek Vantagepoint, MS Excel/Word/Outlook/Bluebeam, and other required programs.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

jobs.description:
At Anchorage Digital, we are building the world’s most advanced digital asset platform for institutions to participate in crypto.
 
Anchorage Digital is a crypto platform that enables institutions to participate in digital assets through custody, staking, trading, governance, settlement, and the industry's leading security infrastructure. Home to Anchorage Digital Bank N.A., the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., Anchorage Digital also serves institutions through Anchorage Digital Singapore, Porto by Anchorage Digital, and other offerings.
 
The company is funded by leading institutions including Andreessen Horowitz, GIC, Goldman Sachs, KKR, and Visa, with its Series D valuation over $3 billion. Founded in 2017 in San Francisco, California, Anchorage Digital has offices in New York, New York; Porto, Portugal; Singapore; and Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Learn more at anchorage.com, on X @Anchorage, and on LinkedIn. 
With the evolving landscape of digital threats and an increasing volume of sophisticated attacks by malicious actors, we have a security policy mandating all new hires complete an in-person onboarding process - no exceptions. Security is our foundation and we prioritize physical identity verification and secure IT setup. While our security and IT logistics require physical presence to protect our infrastructure from sophisticated global threats, this move is equally about our Village culture. We believe that a laptop can be shipped, but our culture cannot.


As a Member of Custody Operations, Digital Assets, you are responsible for supporting the day-to-day operations that the company processes in support of clients' daily activities. In this role, you are responsible for ensuring an excellent operational experience by reviewing client transactions and instructions in a timely manner, providing attentive care to our clients, and managing their transactions in a risk-conscious way. jobs.title: Associate Director/Director, Clinical Contracts
jobs.description:
When our people share why they joined Rapport and love it here, it comes down to three things: the science, the mission, and the team. At Rapport, we’re driven by a passion for developing precision neuromedicines with the potential for fewer side effects, enabling patients and their families to enjoy healthier, more fulfilling lives. And we’re doing this with extraordinary science and awesome people (affectionately called Rapptors).

Our innovative scientific platform is centered on Receptor Associate Proteins (RAPs). RAPs are a component of neuronal receptor complexes, which play a crucial role in regulating receptor assembly and function. This precision approach has the potential to revolutionize the development of small molecule therapies. We are excited about the potential of our lead program, RAP-219. Our first indication targets focal epilepsy with additional clinical trials in primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures (PGTCS) and bipolar disorder.

The strength of Rapport comes from our Rapptors – who are united by our mission to improve patients lives. We bring the heart and hustle to advance our science forward, always staying true to our core values. We hope you’re as excited about this opportunity as we are!

This role is based in Boston, MA with onsite presence required Monday-Wednesday

Your impact:

As our Associate Director or Director of Clinical Contracts, you’ll help turn clinical plans into action. You’ll own clinical trial agreements, site budgets, and vendor contracts while partnering with Clinical Ops, Legal, Finance, and our CROs to keep studies moving. You’ll help build a contracting process that keeps pace with our growing global portfolio.

Your day-to-day:

• Lead end-to-end drafting, review, and negotiation of Confidentiality Disclosure Agreements (CDAs), Master Service Agreements (MSAs), Material Transfer Agreements (MTAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), License Agreements, Subscription Agreements.

• Review and negotiate site Clinical Trial Agreements (CTAs) and CDAs.

• Partner closely with Clinical Operations, outside counsel, Finance, and CRO/vendor teams to align contract terms with study timelines and budget parameters.

• Develop and maintain contract templates, fallback language, and negotiation playbooks to standardize and accelerate the contracting process.

• Track contract status, cycle times, and site activation timelines; proactively identify and resolve bottlenecks.

• Ensure all agreements comply with applicable regulations (FDA, ICH-GCP, GDPR and other privacy regulations), Fair Market Value (FMV) standards, and company policies.

• Mentor and provide guidance to junior contracts staff or coordinators as the team scales.

• Contribute to process improvement initiatives, including contract management systems/tools (e.g., Agiloft, Coupa).

• Maintain accurate, audit-ready contract files and documentation in support of inspection readiness.

Must-Haves:

• Bachelor's degree required

• 8-10+ years of experience reviewing and negotiating clinical trial agreements, and/or related vendor contracts within a biotech, pharmaceutical, or CRO environment.

• Global contract experience, including familiarity with international site contracting and cross-border legal/privacy considerations.

• Deep familiarity with clinical trial agreement structures, and FMV principles.

• Working knowledge of FDA regulations and ICH-GCP guidelines as they pertain to clinical contracting.

• Strong negotiation skills with a track record of driving agreements to execution efficiently.

• Excellent cross-functional collaboration skills, with experience partnering across Legal, Finance, Development, CMC, Quality, Biometrics, Bioanalytics, Regulatory, and Clinical Operations.

• Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage a high volume of contracts simultaneously.

What makes Rapport special:

• Every role has meaning. We’re determined to discover a better way for patients, and you’ll feel the passion from the start.

• We are driven to innovate. Exciting science that pushes boundaries and opens new possibilities.

• Your perspective matters. Stick your neck out, share your ideas – we work as a team.

• We have FUN. We hire smart, dedicated, down-to-earth people that you’ll enjoy spending time with.

• Leadership that CARES – about you, your growth + development.

• We're bicoastal. Whether you're in the lab full-time in San Diego or taking advantage of a more hybrid work schedule in Boston – we make the most of our time together.

• Competitive benefits. Including unlimited PTO, a lifestyle spending account, commuting reimbursement, and much more!

• You get to be YOU! Show up as you are and make every day count.

Your Compensation:

We get it. Compensation is an important part of your offer. You shouldn’t be surprised at the end of the recruiting process, and you should know that your offer is fair and equitable. How do we do this?  We tell you about our hiring range now - we expect the hiring range for the role to be $175,000 to $195,000 for the Associate Director level and $195,000 to $215,000 for the Director level. Our actual offer will reflect a lot of factors including your relevant skills, experience, location, salary market data, and internal equity. In addition to a competitive salary, we also offer a pretty great benefits package. We don’t stop here - if you join Rapport, we go to the next level. We share our full salary ranges for every level across our company.

Hybrid Work Environment:

We prioritize in person connection with our fellow Rapptors! Our team members come together onsite at our Boston office Monday-Wednesday to create more opportunities for innovation, collaboration, and connection.

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Working closely with the Global Mobility Lead, you’ll help strengthen the processes, infrastructure, and vendor relationships that underpin our mobility programs. You’ll have meaningful autonomy to identify gaps, lead improvements, and turn recurring needs into scalable ways of working. As our programs mature, your scope will expand beyond case delivery to include ownership of broader mobility programs, while remaining close to the work and the people we support.







WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the end-to-end delivery of immigration and mobility matters across sponsorship, relocation, cross-border transfers, remote work, and business travel.

 - Lead the company-side strategy and delivery for complex U.S. immigration matters in partnership with outside counsel, independently assessing options, risks, timing, and next steps.

 - Advise candidates, employees, managers, Recruiting, People Business Partners, and business leaders on mobility options and tradeoffs, engaging Legal, Tax, Payroll, Total Rewards, or local experts when needed.

 - Manage relationships with immigration counsel, tax advisors, relocation providers, and other mobility partners, holding them accountable for service, quality, and employee experience.

 - Build and improve the workflows, playbooks, communications, reporting, and self-service resources that make mobility easier to navigate and enable Recruiting and the People team to handle routine questions themselves.

 - Maintain accurate work authorization and mobility data, support applicable immigration, right-to-work, and audit-readiness requirements, and apply our sponsorship and mobility policies consistently — surfacing exceptions and escalations with a clear recommendation.

 - Guide candidates and employees through complex and often stressful situations with clarity, responsiveness, discretion, and empathy.
   
   


WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 5–8 years of progressive global mobility experience, including meaningful experience in an in-house corporate mobility role.

 - Deep, practical knowledge of U.S. employment-based immigration, with the ability to independently assess options, pressure-test outside counsel’s recommendations, and translate legal advice into clear business guidance.

 - Demonstrated experience operating as a trusted mobility advisor to employees, managers, and cross-functional partners.

 - Experience across the broader mobility lifecycle, including relocation, cross-border transfers, remote work, and business travel, with a holistic understanding of how these matters intersect.

 - Working knowledge of the tax, compensation, payroll, benefits, equity, and employment considerations surrounding cross-border moves, together with the judgment to identify risks and engage the right specialists.

 - Experience independently managing a portfolio of complex, time-sensitive matters and exercising sound judgment with incomplete information.

 - Experience managing outside counsel and mobility vendors, setting clear expectations, driving service quality, and improving operations through documentation, automation, AI-enabled tools, or reporting.

 - Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish credibility, influence decisions, and explain requirements clearly and empathetically.

 - A collaborative, hands-on approach and comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where priorities, programs, and ways of working continue to evolve.

Nice to Have

 - Experience coordinating employment-based immigration matters outside the United States through local counsel, with direct knowledge of immigration requirements in one or more additional regions.

 - Experience helping build or scale mobility programs in a high-growth, globally expanding company.







COMPENSATION

$100,500 - $138,200 USD

jobs.title: Application Security Engineer
jobs.description:
How You’ll Make An Impact

At Strive Health, patients come first. We’re on a mission to transform chronic conditions by identifying risk earlier, coordinating thoughtful care, and supporting people through every stage of their health journey.

Our work reduces emergency visits, improves outcomes, and helps patients live fuller lives. You’ll work alongside passionate Strivers who care deeply about making an impact, show up for one another as One Team, and find ways to elevate the everyday.

If you’re looking for meaningful work where your contributions truly matter, you’ll feel right at home at Strive!

Benefits & Perks

• Hybrid-Remote Flexibility – Work from home while fulfilling in-person needs at the office, clinic, or patient home visits.

• Comprehensive Benefits – Medical, dental, and vision insurance, employee assistance programs, employer-paid and voluntary life and disability insurance, plus health and flexible spending accounts.

• Financial & Retirement Support – Competitive compensation with a performance-based bonus program, 401k with employer match, and financial wellness resources.

• Time Off & Leave – Paid holidays, vacation time, sick time, and paid birthgiving, bonding, sabbatical, and living donor leaves.

• Wellness & Growth – Family forming services through Maven Maternity at no cost and physical wellness perks, mental health support, and an annual professional development stipend.

To learn more about our offerings, click here.

What You’ll Do

The Application Security Engineer is responsible for embedding application security directly into Strive’s product development lifecycle, specifically supporting the deployment of Canvas Medical, patient-facing experiences, and future mobile applications. You will serve as the primary security partner for Product and Engineering, ensuring that applications are built securely from the design phase through to production. Rather than treating security as a late-stage penetration test, you will establish the requirements, review gates, testing frameworks, and remediation operating rhythms necessary to support a secure and compliant development pipeline.

The Day to Day

Security Discovery and Threat Modeling:

• Perform threat modeling and establish a security baseline for internal environments, patient portals, mobile applications, and integration services.

• Maintain data-flow and trust-boundary diagrams, assessing identity, operational, and PHI data classifications.

Architecture & Secure Product Development:

• Collaborate with engineering teams to embed security acceptance criteria into PRDs, technical plans, and Jira stories.

• Conduct architecture reviews focusing on tenant boundaries, server-side authorization, prevention of IDOR (insecure direct object references), and lateral movement guardrails.

• Develop and enforce merge request (MR) checklists covering authentication, input validation, secrets management, and cryptography.

Application Security Testing Framework:

• Design, deploy, and operate application security testing tools including SAST, DAST, Software Composition Analysis (SCA), and container/IaC scanning.

• Perform authenticated testing of browser workflows and APIs (e.g., using Burp Suite Enterprise).

• Conduct manual testing for complex vulnerabilities such as privilege escalation, SSRF, and business-logic abuse.

Vulnerability Management & Remediation:

• Manage the vulnerability intake pipeline, assign severities, and track remediation aligned with internal SLAs.

• Lead recurring vulnerability review sessions with Security, Product, and Engineering stakeholders.

• Coordinate external penetration tests, including scoping, vendor selection, and tracking of remediation/retesting.

Compliance & Audit Readiness:

• Ensure all security requirements, threat models, testing evidence, and remediation documentation align with internal compliance needs (e.g., HITRUST, SOC 2).

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field.

• 3+ years (Engineer) to 5+ years (Senior) of experience in information security, with a strong focus on Application Security, DevSecOps, or software engineering.

• Demonstrable experience integrating security tools into CI/CD pipelines (e.g., SAST, DAST, SCA).

• Experience leading or performing application threat modeling, architecture reviews, and manual security testing.

• Familiarity with securing cloud environments (SaaS, IaaS, PaaS) and understanding of cloud architecture.

• Internet Connectivity - Min Speeds: 3.8Mbps/3.0Mbps (up/down): Latency <60 ms.

• Ability to travel and be onsite to meet business needs.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience within the healthcare sector, securing environments that manage PHI and complying with frameworks like HITRUST.

• Deep expertise in identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10, IDOR, SSRF, authentication bypass).

• Experience with testing and securing complex API integrations, mobile application releases, and web-based portals.

• Familiarity with enterprise dynamic testing tools (e.g., Burp Suite Enterprise) and automating security testing against deployed applications.

• Advanced certifications in application security or information security (e.g., CSSLP, GWAPT, CISSP, CEH).

About You

• Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, able to assess complex application security issues and provide practical, developer-friendly solutions.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills; capable of articulating technical risk to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Proactive and adaptable, comfortable embedding directly with engineering pods to shift security “left”.

Annual Salary Range: $108,500 - $136,000. This position is also eligible for a target annual bonus of 10%

Final compensation will be determined based on location, experience, and qualifications.
